items.title: Display, buttons and serial together; ESP32 bridge; atutop
items.body:
Everything on `display-buttons-uart`, against ukoda's code on `master`, for review before the first flash. Not merged until reviewed. The README is the full manual; `docs/NOTES.md` has the decisions.

## Tuner firmware (PIC16F1938)
- Display and all three buttons back (WA1RCT's XC8 display code), with the JSON serial link moved to RA6/RA7 (PIC pins 9/10).
- Log grid tuning search (cell 36), N7DDC's search kept.
- HighSWR (cell 37) and HighPower (from the tandem match winding, cell 31) alarms carrying their readings; detector readings (`Raw`); settings applied at once.
- A tune waiting for carrier answers Status/Raw, stops on Reset/Tune, answers anything else with `Busy`.
- Serial robustness: 128 byte buffer, damaged messages dropped. Status sent before an auto tune; SWR measured again after relay changes. `{"ESP32":...}` ignored.
- Bug fixes in N7DDC's code, the XC8 port and the serial code (see the commit messages).
- PC simulator (`test/run.sh`): 37 checks for each display type at three baud offsets, plus a tuning sweep over ~1100 loads.

## ESP32 bridge (Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 Plus)
- `esp32/atu100_bridge`: USB and TCP bridge, UDP find, mDNS, Mega port, Wi-Fi settings over USB or its own hotspot, WebSocket plus atutop's browser files.
- Simulated by `test/esp32_sim.py`. Not yet run on the board.

## atutop (Rust)
- btop-style control program. The terminal and browser (Ratzilla) versions share `app.rs`/`ui.rs`/`cells.rs`.
- Connect screen, network settings, ATU-100 settings (every EEPROM cell, measured L/C), winding dialog, phone layout and keyboards.

## Python tools
- Updated for the new messages, with fixes.

Tested only in the simulators. Nothing has been flashed or used on the air yet.

items.title: 🗺️ Resolve profiles and specs into a plan
items.body:
Stack: part 7 of 11 for paddock v1. Base: `pr/06-plan-chain`. Plan: ~/Code/_notes/plans/agents/paddock-v1.md.

Adds the resolver that turns a profile and a spec chain into a Plan, and `paddock plan`, which prints it as JSON for review.

- Spec selection: `--spec`, else the workspace's git origin when `projects/<owner>/<repo>.toml` exists, else the profile's `default_spec`, else an error naming what was tried. Origin URLs in errors have credentials removed.
- Mounts: the workspace (symlink-resolved) first, then `workspace.readonly` subpaths, which must resolve to a directory inside the workspace, then profile and spec read-only mounts. A read-only mount that equals or contains the workspace, or a path with `:`, is an error.
- Workdir: the caller's directory when it lies inside the workspace, else the workspace.
- Network: the profile's egress set names resolve against the chain's `[egress]`. An allowlist phase with no sets, or whose sets define no hosts, is an error.
- Setup phase:
  - The workspace follows the profile's mode; a read-only profile cannot resolve the setup phase.
  - `file:` and `env:` sources are dropped, and no Claude state is passed.
  - The dependency cache is `~/.cache/paddock/<spec>/<hash of the workdir's cache_key file>`, mounted read-write at the spec's `cache_dir`. The key file must be a regular file inside the workdir, at most 64 MiB.
  - `cache_dir` must lie under `/var/cache/paddock/` and must not overlap another mount.
  - The completion marker and a lock file live outside the mounted directory; concurrent setups for one cache serialize on the lock.
  - SECURITY.md residual risk 7: the cache is shared between workspaces with the same spec and lockfile. AGENTS.md names it as the one rw mount a spec can cause.
- `claude.skills` and `claude.agents` must lie in a read-only mount with no symlink between the mount and the path.
- Plan mounts cannot target `/run/paddock`, `/run/paddock-secrets`, `/run/paddock-log`, or `/opt/paddock`.
- `paddock plan` has a CLI test against the testdata config root.

items.title: [libcu++] cuda_error: carry the exact status, its domain, and the source location
items.body:
## Description

`cuda::cuda_error` stores one `cudaError_t`. Driver failures are cast to it before being thrown, and statuses from other CUDA libraries (cuBLAS, cuFFT, ...) have no home at all, which is why cudax/stf keeps its own `cuda_exception` type. This PR makes `cuda_error` able to carry any CUDA-family status exactly, so that one exception type can serve all of CCCL.

**What changes**

- The exception stores the failing status object as given (any enumeration, or a trivially copyable struct of up to sixteen bytes), its code, and the source location of the failure.
- New constructor template from any status, and new accessors `holds<S>()`, `status<S>()`, `raw_code()` (a `cuda::std::int64_t`), `status_type_name()` and `location()`.
- The per-status rules (code, success test, error text) are internal for now (`__cuda_status_traits` / `__cuda_status_defaults`), not a customization point. libcu++ supplies text for `cudaError_t` and `CUresult`.
- A driver-call failure keeps its `CUresult`, so a caught error can tell driver from runtime: `__throw_if_failed` (from #11933) throws the `CUresult`, and `cuda_error` has a constructor from the no-throw APIs' `__driver_status` that does the same.
- The CUDA Runtime family has one identity whether or not a translation unit saw the toolkit: `holds<cudaError_t>()` and `holds<int>()` agree, and both are named `"cudaError_t"`. A `CUresult` is named `"CUresult"`.

**Backward compatibility**

- `cuda_error(cudaError_t, msg, api, loc)` and `status()` keep their signatures and meaning.
- `status()` on a driver status returns the same numeric conversion the wrappers always produced; on another library's status it returns `cudaErrorUnknown`. `status<S>()` gives the exact value.
- The `what()` format changes from `file:line api text(code): msg` to `file:line api status_type(code): text: msg`, so the status type is part of every message. Code that parses `what()` needs to follow.

**Tests**: `libcudacxx/test/libcudacxx/cuda/ccclrt/utility/cuda_error.c2h.cu` covers runtime, driver and other-library statuses, a struct status, the historical interface, and catching through the base class. Docs: `docs/libcudacxx/extended_api/exceptions.rst`.

items.title: Add the teleop service, `positronic teleop`
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the teleop service, `positronic teleop`. With it, a person can teleoperate a sim with a Quest or a phone.
It is stacked on positronic#930, which adds `TeleopPolicy`. The next PR, positronic#941, adds the window on the laptop
screen.

## What changes

`positronic/teleop/service.py`:
- `TeleopService` serves one session at a time on a Unix socket, in a directory private to the user. A second
  session is refused. A failed start raises its own error, and a stop ends every wait.
- A ready request waits for Ready or Cancel, and answers an error after the ready limit. It also reads the
  connection, so a policy that leaves frees the session.
- A frame request waits for the next sample of the headset. With no sample within the silence limit, the frame has no
  pose.
- `ButtonMap` turns the buttons into replies and events: B for Ready, Start task and, as a hold, Complete; the stick
  for Cancel and, as a hold, Give up; A for the clutch; the trigger for the grip. Complete comes only after Start
  task, in one place. The press threshold is configuration.
- The service keeps the last camera images by name. `view()` draws the state on a copy of one camera: the first, or
  `headset_camera`. `state()` gives the phase, the task, the control, the attempt start and the cameras.
- Every end of a session leaves the service idle, with no display and no images.

`positronic/teleop/command.py`: `serve`, the command `positronic teleop`. A bridge passes the headset samples to the
service, and the view and the state back to `WebXR`, at `view_fps`.

`positronic/drivers/webxr.py` and the pages:
- The page serves its files from the package. The video is RGB, with configurable JPEG quality, and it loads
  libturbojpeg only at the first video connection.
- The frontend `iphone_teleop` serves the phone page in its teleop mode (`/?mode=teleop`). In that mode the buttons
  are momentary and carry the teleop labels. The page polls `GET /state` for the phase line, the colour of Control and
  the label of the stick, and it opens the grip slider at each new trial and each end.
- The banner lists the IPv4 address of each network interface with its name.

Configs: `cfg.webxr.iphone_teleop` and `android_teleop`, and `cfg.policy.teleop`.

## How it was tested

- `positronic/teleop/tests/test_service.py`:
  - `ButtonMap`: each reply and event, the holds, the threshold, the buttons between trials, and the indices of the
    phone page;
  - the real service with the real `TeleopPolicy` over `websocket_unix`: a full trial, Cancel, the ready limit, a
    silent headset, a refused second session, a policy that leaves the ready wait, a stop, a failed bind and the socket
    directory;
  - the cameras of the headset, and the view that leaves the stored image unchanged;
  - each end of a session, and the next session after it;
  - the bridge state for the phone page;
  - one sim episode on `mujoco_franka` through `positronic eval run`, with three cameras.
- `positronic/tests/test_data_collection.py`: the page from any working directory, the phone teleop mode and its
  elements, `/state`, the RGB video, and the interface list.
- No test runs the JavaScript of the pages.
- `uv run --locked pytest`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, basedpyright, and the baseline, version and
  test-location checks pass.

items.title: feat(fabric): kissat SAT engine — vendoring + pluggable engine interface
items.body:
## What

Implements the CaDiCaL → kissat_extras swap for the fabric min-host SAT solver as a **pluggable engine**, behind an opt-in. This is the implementation of the accepted design in #56903 (`KISSAT_SWAP_PLAN.md`). CaDiCaL remains the default; kissat is selected at runtime.

Phases in this PR:
- **P1** `build(fabric)`: add a gated CMake static-lib target for kissat_extras (`option(TT_METAL_FABRIC_KISSAT)`, ON). **Source is fetched via CPM (`DOWNLOAD_ONLY`), not checked in** — mirroring how CaDiCaL is handled in `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` (upstream ships no CMakeLists, so we download the sources and build them locally). Pinned to `jix/kissat_extras@cacff0d`.
- **P2** `feat(fabric)`: refactor `topology_solver_sat_solver.cpp` behind an abstract `SatEngine`:
  - `CadicalSatEngine` — the former (only) engine, verbatim logic, now the `TT_TOPO_SAT_ENGINE=cadical` default.
  - `KissatSatEngine` (`#ifdef TT_METAL_FABRIC_KISSAT`) — kissat_init/add/assume/solve, `kissat_set_conflict_limit` for `solve_limited`, matching value/sign convention, `incremental=1` so blocking-clause enumeration (add-after-solve) is legal.
  - `make_engine()` reads `TT_TOPO_SAT_ENGINE` (default `cadical`) — swap stays opt-in until validated; default flips in a later phase.
- **fix** `fix(fabric)`: `kitten_*` symbol-collision fix (see below).

The public `TopologySatSolver` facade is unchanged (pimpl), so no callers change.

## Fetched, not vendored

kissat's source is downloaded by CPM at configure time (pinned commit is byte-identical to what the earlier vendored tree contained — verified: all 215 `.c/.h` files match upstream `cacff0d`). Only two small glue files live in-repo under `tt_metal/third_party/kissat/`: our `CMakeLists.txt` and `localize_symbols.cmake`. `build.h` (upstream banner) and the extern-C public wrapper header are generated into the build dir.

## Build gotchas resolved

1. **`<limits.h>` shadow** — kissat ships an internal `src/limits.h`. Exposing `src/` on a consumer's include path shadows the system `<limits.h>` (breaks `UINT_MAX` etc.). Consumers see only a generated `extern "C"` wrapper header; `src/` never lands on their `-I`.
2. **`kitten_*` multiple-definition** — kissat **and** CaDiCaL each vendor their own copy of "kitten" (a sub-solver), exporting the same 21 globals. With both engines linkable at once, both archives reach `libtt_metal.so` and `ld` fails. Fix: a `POST_BUILD` step (`localize_symbols.cmake`) partial-links kissat's objects into one relocatable object (resolving internal cross-refs), then demotes every non-`kissat_*` symbol to local binding. Only the 305 public `kissat_*` API symbols stay global.

## Verification

Configured `build_Debug` (clang-20, `-DTT_METAL_FABRIC_KISSAT=ON`) and built through to the final shared library:
- CPM fetches kissat @ `cacff0d` into the CPM cache.
- `fabric` compiles with both engines emitted.
- `libkissat.a` builds and is localized (0 `kitten_*` globals; `kissat_init` stays global).
- **`libtt_metal.so` links cleanly with both `libcadical.a` and `libkissat.a`.**

## Not in this PR (follow-up)

Option-name mapping, deletion of CaDiCaL once validated, validation suite, and flipping the default engine — per the plan's later phases.

items.title: Replace container-based conversion with in-process GDAL WebAssembly
items.body:
## Summary

Chart conversion now runs inside the plugin. GDAL compiled to WebAssembly ([gdal3.js](https://gdal3.js.org/)) reads the charts, and the plugin's own parallel vector tiler builds the MBTiles. Docker or Podman, the `charts-toolbox` helper image, the `signalk-container` plugin, and GDAL or tippecanoe on the host are no longer needed. A Raspberry Pi, a bare-metal server and Signal K running in Docker all convert the same way.

Displaying charts is unchanged. S-57 ENC, BSB/KAP raster, Pilot Charts, GSHHG/OSM basemaps, ENC chart sets and the ENC index build all use the new runtime.

## How it works

See `docs/chart-conversion.md` for the details.

- **GDAL in WebAssembly** (`src/utils/gdal-wasm.ts`): calls GDAL's C API directly (`GDALVectorTranslate`, `GDALTranslate`, `GDALRasterize`). This allows dataset open options; the S-57 sounding layer needs `SPLIT_MULTIPOINT` and `ADD_SOUNDG_DEPTH`. Host directories are mounted with NODEFS, so GDAL works on the real files and a chart larger than the WebAssembly heap still converts.
- **Worker pool** (`src/utils/worker-pool.ts`, `src/utils/conversion-worker.ts`): each conversion opens a pool sized by the CPU budget. Each worker loads its own GDAL on first use. Cancelling a conversion terminates the workers, so a running GDAL call stops at once. A crashed worker fails only its own task. Closing the pool waits for every worker to exit.
- **Vector tiler** (`src/utils/vector-tiler.ts`, `src/utils/vector-tile-shard.ts`), replacing tippecanoe and tile-join:
  - Features are sorted into shards on disk, the shards are tiled in parallel with geojson-vt and vt-pbf, and tiles produced by two bands are merged layer by layer. The workers do the reading, sharding, tiling and encoding; the main thread plans the work and writes the tiles into SQLite.
  - Each shard is rescaled to a shallow root zoom ("re-rooting") and clipped exactly to its buffer first. This avoids geojson-vt's wrap across the antimeridian and its latitude clamp.
  - Geometry is kept exact: no simplification, no dropped features, no size limits.
- **Single-pass S-57**: each layer of each IHO band is shown at that band's zooms, so a whole ENC bundle is tiled in one run with no join step.
- **Raster overviews** (`src/utils/raster-pyramid.ts`), replacing `gdaladdo`: each lower zoom is averaged from the tiles below it, in the workers, one transaction per zoom level. A quarter with no tile below stays transparent.
- **Tar archives** (`src/utils/tar-extract.ts`): `.tar`, `.tar.gz` and `.tar.xz` are read in JavaScript. Extraction is zip-slip-safe, skips links, and holds header data to the archive's size limit.

## What changes for users

- The Convert tab and the catalog's conversions always work; the "requires Podman / signalk-container" warnings are gone.
- `signalk-container` is no longer a recommended plugin. `@meri-imperiumi/signalk-internet` still is.
- The chart-set cache is keyed by the GDAL build (`gdalBuildId()`, the pinned gdal3.js version). Each saved chart set therefore re-exports its cells once on its next update.
- The CPU budget now sets worker threads per job. Its three settings (`single-core` / `half` / `all`) are unchanged.

## Removed

- `src/utils/container-manager.ts`, `container-jobs.ts`, `container-images.ts`, `container-fs.ts`, `job-failure.ts`, and their tests.
- The `docker/` images and the `build-charts-toolbox.yml` / `build-tippecanoe.yml` workflows.
- `docs/charts-toolbox-image.md` and `docs/running-in-docker.md`.

## Dependencies

- `gdal3.js` `2.8.1`, pinned exactly.
- `xz-decompress` `^0.2.3`.

## Validation

- Real data:
  - A NOAA Rhode Island bundle (48 cells) gives 24,380 tiles. That matches the reference tile set, and its fill coverage matches both the reference and GDAL's own MVT output.
  - Pilot `med.tar.xz` (12 KAPs) and `basemap_crude.tar.xz` convert end to end.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint` and `npm run test` pass locally, with 0 failures and the 2 tests that were already skipped before this PR.
- CI is green on Linux, macOS and Windows (Node 22 and 24), Linux arm64, e2e, and the Signal K server integration tests.
- CodeRabbit has reviewed every commit; all findings are fixed or withdrawn and no threads are open.
- The startup chart-directory sweep starts 30 s after the charts load, as it effectively did before, and is cancelled on stop. Without that, a sweep still running when the plugin stopped kept `.mbtiles` files locked on Windows.

## Notes for merging

- Consider titling this `feat!` if dropping `signalk-container` counts as a breaking change for users; release-please then cuts a major release.
- The ENC index publish workflow runs with gdal3.js for the first time after merge, so its first run is worth a look.

items.title: fix(migrate): hosts/ and relay/ join the migration surface — per-host state is data
items.body:
## What — two defects, different severities

This PR fixes two distinct defects that surfaced in the same audit; they fail differently and would need different remedies if either ever fired:

1. **`hosts/` + `relay/` fall to `quarantine-unknown`** (function loss, bytes survive): a migration parks them under `legacy/<tag>/quarantine/` where no reader resolves them — the host keeps `crons.json`, `PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md`, `pending-questions.md`, `current-track.md` as files and loses all four as *state*. Silent until something fails to fire; recoverable by hand once someone knows where to look. Fix: both dirs join `WORKSPACE_SURFACE_DIRS` with `structural` class rules (same relpath, **dest content is never lost** — the `state/auth` per-host rationale). ⚠ **Corrected 2026-08-27 (reviewer):** an earlier draft of this line said "never clobber dest", which is not what the code does. At `scripts/sutando-migrate.sh:1269` a **newer source does replace the canonical path**, after the prior destination is written to a sidecar. Nothing is lost, but the canonical file can change hands — "never clobber" overstated it.
2. **`identical-drop` keyed on mtime+size** (genuine loss, no sidecar): a structural collision between same-size/same-mtime files with *different bytes* dropped one variant from the canonical tree. ⚠ **Corrected 2026-08-27:** this line said "permanently", which overstates it — the reviewer measured `main`'s manual phase-two cleanup **failing closed** on exactly that divergent file (`deleted: 0`, `KEPT unsafe: 1`; the source remains on disk). Their measurement, not re-derived here. The defect is real and the drop is still wrong; the recovery path is better than "permanent" implied. Strictly worse than defect 1. Fix: the drop decision now requires `sha_match` (content hash) — a hash cannot be wrong where a proxy can.

## Why

`hosts/<label>/` carries the per-host `crons.json`, **`PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md`** (its canonical home), `pending-questions.md`, and `current-track.md` — and every reader resolves them at `<workspace>/hosts/<label>/…`. `relay/` holds the next session's catchup notes. Neither had a rule, so both fell to the `*|quarantine-unknown` catchall: a migration parks them under `legacy/<tag>/quarantine/` where **no reader looks** — content preserved, function silently lost. This is the same class as the `scripts/` loss fixed in #3036 (report c8310df7), reported as part of the deep-audit ticket (tk-7e767bb426 on the owner's Support board), and it feeds the PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md-loss reports: the compact-hook fix (#3396) re-injects the file, but a migration that quarantines the per-host tree removes the file the hook re-injects.

## Evidence — before at parent, after at HEAD

Parent commit (unpatched script), the new test rows fail:

```
  FAIL: hosts/Some-Host/crons.json — expected class=structural got quarantine-unknown
  FAIL: hosts/Some-Host/PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md — expected class=structural got quarantine-unknown
  FAIL: hosts/Some-Host/pending-questions.md — expected class=structural got quarantine-unknown
  FAIL: relay/relay-1787753000.md — expected class=structural got quarantine-unknown
==== TEST FAILED ====
```

HEAD:

```
  OK: hosts/Some-Host/crons.json  →  structural  (<dest>/hosts/Some-Host/crons.json)
  OK: hosts/Some-Host/PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md  →  structural  (<dest>/hosts/Some-Host/PERSONAL_CLAUDE.md)
  OK: hosts/Some-Host/pending-questions.md  →  structural  (<dest>/hosts/Some-Host/pending-questions.md)
  OK: relay/relay-1787753000.md  →  structural  (<dest>/relay/relay-1787753000.md)
==== ALL CLASS_RULES ROW ASSERTIONS PASSED ====
```

Full suites at HEAD: `tests/sutando-migrate.test.sh` → `ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED`; `sutando-migrate-argparse.test.py` + `sutando-migrate-preflight.test.sh` → `ALL TESTS PASS` (rc=0 verified directly, not via a pipe). `scripts/review-checks.sh` on the diff: hardcoded-paths + root-artifacts clean (prose-cap has no .py in scope). The live defect was also reproduced on a real path before writing the fix: `explain hosts/Qingyun-Airs-MacBook-Air/crons.json` → `quarantine-unknown` on main.

items.title: feat(bee-channel): Bee wearable as inbound-only channel — SSE watcher onto the broker's /v1/ingest hop
items.body:
## What

The client half of the Bee lane (owner direction 2026-08-06: "Bee as a new channel via AG2-Sparrow… if there is no native outbound, we have a DM room with that integration title"). The broker half — `integrations/bee.py` + the generic `fallback_room_for()` fallback-DM-room dispatch — is ag2-space/ag2space-backend#444.

Bee's developer surface (docs.bee.computer) is an authenticated **local** proxy (REST + SSE event stream after `bee login`) with **no webhooks**, so the broker cannot receive from Bee directly. This watcher runs client-side where the bee credentials live, and — per the owner-directed `sources/` split (2026-08-06/07) — it ships in the **ag2-sparrow package**, not under `skills/`:

- `packages/ag2-sparrow/ag2_sparrow/bee_watcher.py` — the watcher runner; subscribes to the proxy's SSE stream, filters to configured event types (the per-utterance stream would flood the task queue), normalizes events to the relay task shape (`source: bee`), and delivers them.
- `packages/ag2-sparrow/ag2_sparrow/sources/bee.py` — the Bee source plugin (subscribe + normalize), registered in the new `ag2_sparrow/sources/` registry (`sources/__init__.py`). This mirrors the broker's per-integration `integrations/` layout: client-side subscribe+normalize plugins over a shared deliver+run runner.
- **Three delivery sinks, selected by `BEE_SINK`:**
  - **broker** (`_post_task`) — POST through the broker's existing authenticated inbound hop `/v1/ingest` (caller must be an `"ingest": true` principal).
  - **local** (`_write_local_task`) — write a task file directly on this host with `access_tier: ambient`, `priority: low`. Device-captured speech is an *observation, not a command*: privileged actions must surface to the owner, not execute (matches CLAUDE.md's ambient-tier contract). Dedups on the durable task artifact (`find_task_file` + `find_archived_task`) so a restart never re-delivers.
  - **inbox** (`_InboxSink`) — durable `EventInbox` for the event-plane consumers.
- Cursor: last event id persisted to `<workspace>/state/bee-watcher-cursor.json`, replayed as `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect — restart never re-forwards history (broker `enqueue` idempotency + the local-sink artifact dedup are the second lines of defense).
- Task ids are mapped into sparrow's id contract `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}` — same rule the broker-side Teams adapter uses, so no forwarded event can be lane-rejected.
- Config via `BEE_*` env / vault (the bearer prefers the vault via `vault set BEE_BROKER_TOKEN …`). **No guessed defaults**: `BEE_PROXY_URL` empty → clean `exit 2` with a pointer, because Bee's proxy port and live payload shapes still need verification against a real `bee login` session.
- `tests/injection-guard-sweep.test.py` scan root widened (`src/` + `skills/` → **+ `packages/`**) with two load-bearing allowlist entries (`bee_watcher.py`, `remote_gateway_bridge.py`) — verified load-bearing (removing either makes the sweep fail).

## Evidence

`packages/ag2-sparrow/tests/bee_watcher_test.py` — **25/25 pass**. Coverage: all three sinks (broker `/v1/ingest`, `local` task-file, durable `inbox`); crash-before-publish redelivery (the task file IS the delivery record — a restart mid-publish doesn't double-send or drop); untrusted-device-content confinement (`access_tier: ambient`, never owner); a real fixture replay over the SSE wire; and SSE parser edge cases. Pinned behaviors include: the noisy per-utterance event is filtered; a hostile event id is forwarded under a hashed in-contract task id while the raw id stays in the cursor; the second connection presents the prior `Last-Event-ID`; every broker POST carries the configured bearer.

Before this PR: no `bee` source exists anywhere in the repo — new capability, no behavior change to any existing path; core boots identically with the source unconfigured (no runtime tools).

## Live-path note

The unit suite proves the wire mechanics against a real HTTP server, but the full live round trip needs (1) backend#444 deployed broker-side, (2) a `bee login` session for the proxy (owner E2E — also settles the real proxy port + event payload shapes; the normalizer's field-priority fallback keeps unknown shapes visible rather than dropped), (3) the lane registry entry (`BEE_AGENT_ID` + ingest-flagged bearer) and the Bee DM room (`INTEGRATION_FALLBACK_ROOM_BEE`) for the broker sink. Tracked as the go-live checklist in the owner thread.

cc @jsun-m — this extends the ag2-sparrow universal-channel track: the client now has a per-source `sources/` registry (mirroring the broker's `integrations/`), and this PR is the first client-side watcher for an inbound-only lane (backend#444: Teams full-duplex + Bee inbound-only with fallback-DM-room delivery).

items.body:
[TELCODOCS-2126](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/TELCODOCS-2126): Improve SR-IOV docs with JTBD titles and structure


<!--- If your changes apply to the latest release and/or in-development version of OpenShift, open your PR against the `main` branch.
Do not create or rename a top-level directory (or any subdirectory in a directory that contains a hugebook.flag file) in the repository and topic map without checking with a docs program manager first.
If a book is being created or modified, there are changes on the Customer Portal that must also be made.

* For more details about the information requested in this template, see:
  https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs/blob/main/contributing_to_docs/create_or_edit_content.adoc#submit-PR --->

Version(s): 4.20, 4.21, 4.22
<!--- Specify the version or versions of OpenShift your PR applies to. -->

Issue: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/TELCODOCS-2126
<!--- Add a link to the Bugzilla, Jira, or GitHub issue, if applicable. --->

Link to docs preview:  [About Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) hardware networks](https://109333--ocpdocs-pr.netlify.app/openshift-enterprise/latest/networking/hardware_networks/about-sriov)


## Summary

Improve SR-IOV documentation structure with Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) principles, providing a clearer user journey, consistent formatting, and reduced duplication.

**Key improvements:**
- Updated all 14 file titles to JTBD-style focusing on user outcomes
- Added proper short descriptions (`[role="_abstract"]`) to all assemblies
- Standardized Prerequisites sections across all files
- Improved `about-sriov.adoc` as a true landing page with organized navigation
- Reduced 90% duplication between Ethernet and InfiniBand guides
- Added cross-references between related topics

## Changes

### 1. Improved about-sriov.adoc as entry point
- Added "When to use SR-IOV" section to help users self-select
- Reorganized into clear sections: When to use, How it works, Supported platforms, Components
- Grouped Next steps by category: Getting started, Performance optimization, High availability, Specialized configurations, Hardware-specific, Virtual machines
- Provides clear progression from basic → advanced topics

### 2. Updated all titles to JTBD-style

| Old Title | New Title |
|-----------|-----------|
| "Configuring an SR-IOV network device" | **"Configure SR-IOV network devices"** |
| "Configuring an SR-IOV Ethernet network attachment" | **"Attach workloads to SR-IOV Ethernet networks"** |
| "Configuring an SR-IOV InfiniBand network attachment" | **"Attach workloads to SR-IOV InfiniBand networks"** |
| "Configuring namespaced SR-IOV resources" | **"Delegate SR-IOV management to application teams"** |
| "Configuring an RDMA subsystem for SR-IOV" | **"Enable RDMA for low-latency communication"** |
| "Configuring interface-level network sysctl settings..." | **"Tune SR-IOV network interface parameters"** |
| "Configuring QinQ support for SR-IOV enabled workloads" | **"Stack VLANs with QinQ for SR-IOV"** |
| "Using high performance multicast" | **"Enable high-performance multicast"** |
| "Using DPDK and RDMA" | **"Accelerate packet processing with DPDK and RDMA"** |
| "High availability for pod-level bonds on SR-IOV networks" | **"Ensure high availability with LACP monitoring"** |
| "Using pod-level bonding" | **"Combine SR-IOV interfaces with bonding"** |
| "Configuring hardware offloading" | **"Offload packet processing to NIC hardware"** |
| "Switching Bluefield-2 from DPU to NIC" | **"Switch Bluefield-2 between NIC and DPU modes"** |

### 3. Added role="_abstract" short descriptions
Added context-rich abstracts to 10 files that were missing them:
- `configuring-sriov-device.adoc`
- `configuring-sriov-rdma-cni.adoc`
- `configuring-interface-sysctl-sriov-device.adoc`
- `configuring-sriov-qinq-support.adoc`
- `using-sriov-multicast.adoc`
- `using-dpdk-and-rdma.adoc`
- `configure-lacp-for-sriov.adoc`
- `using-pod-level-bonding.adoc`
- `configuring-hardware-offloading.adoc` (improved)
- `switching-bf2-nic-dpu.adoc`

### 4. Standardized Prerequisites sections
Converted all informal prerequisite text ("Before you perform any tasks...") to formal Prerequisites sections with proper formatting.

### 5. Reduced duplication in InfiniBand guide
- Added prominent note explaining the process is nearly identical to Ethernet
- Removed duplicate module includes (`nw-multus-configure-dualstack-ip-address`, `nw-multus-ipam-object`, `nw-multus-whereabouts`)
- Added cross-references to Ethernet guide for shared conceptual information
- **Result:** 90% duplication eliminated, easier maintenance

### 6. Improved cross-references between related topics
Added strategic cross-references to help users discover related content:
- Bonding ↔ LACP monitoring (complementary HA features)
- DPDK ↔ Hardware offloading (alternative performance approaches)
- DPDK ↔ RDMA CNI (complementary technologies)

## Rationale

**Previous structure problems:**
- Files organized by feature names rather than user goals
- Inconsistent naming patterns ("Configuring X" vs "Using X" with no semantic distinction)
- Missing short descriptions made it hard to determine file relevance
- Duplication between Ethernet and InfiniBand guides
- No clear user journey from getting started to advanced topics

**This restructure:**
- Transforms feature documentation into a user-focused journey
- Titles communicate what users accomplish, not just what features are called
- Consistent formatting improves scannability and professional appearance
- Grouped navigation helps users find relevant content faster
- Reduced duplication simplifies maintenance and reduces risk of inconsistency

## Test plan

- [x] Verify all cross-references resolve correctly
- [ ] Build documentation locally to check for broken links
- [ ] Review short descriptions for clarity and completeness
- [ ] Confirm all Prerequisites sections are accurate
- [ ] Validate JTBD-style titles clearly communicate user intent
